memoryText: In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Matthew 5:16 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse comes at the end of Jesus’ picture of his followers as the light of the world. It tells us what the light is for.

“In the same way.” Jesus has just said that a lamp is not lit and hidden under a basket but put on a stand to give light to all in the house. His followers are like that. The point of a light is to be seen, and the point of being seen is to help others find their way.

“Let your light shine.” The light is not manufactured. Jesus has already said, “You are the light of the world.” The light comes from him, and he says elsewhere, “I am the light of the world.” We reflect what we have received. Our task is not to produce it but to let it be seen and not to hide it out of fear or embarrassment.

“Before others.” Faith is not private only. It is lived in front of people, at work, at home, among neighbors. Others notice how we treat people, how we handle trouble, and how we speak.

“So that they may see your good works.” The good works are real, practical acts of love and honesty. They are the visible side of a changed heart.

“And give glory to your Father who is in heaven.” This is the goal. The aim of shining is not that people admire us, but that they look past us to the Father. Good works are windows, not mirrors. If someone praises you today, pass it up to him.
weekInReview: This week you walked through the opening of Matthew and the heart of the Sermon on the Mount. You saw Jesus’ birth announced with the name that means “the LORD saves,” the baptism where the Father called him his beloved Son, and the wilderness where Jesus beat the devil by quoting Scripture. In the Sermon, Jesus described the blessed life of kingdom people in the Beatitudes, called you salt and light, and showed what the law really demands: a clean heart, not just clean hands. He taught you to pray, to give and fast in secret, and to trust the Father instead of worrying. Then he asked you to choose between two roads and two foundations. Psalm 1 gave the same choice in older words.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said the poor in spirit are blessed. What would it look like for you to come to God this week with empty hands?
The Sermon shows that the law reaches the heart. In light of that, how does the gospel, that Christ fulfilled the law for us, change the way you read these chapters?
Jesus invites us to call God “Our Father.” What difference does it make to your prayer life, your worries, and your sense of identity to know that?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to let your light shine so that others give him glory.
Thank Jesus for fulfilling the law in your place.
Thank him that you can call him Father.
